take_homes: Don't split into several agents without a reason. The reasons are different access, different language or different stance, and one good prompt is often enough.
The weak spot is the handoff between agents, and the review checks how they worked together, not whether the result is true.
Separate agents with separate access is the argument I would use with my DPO and the works council for anything touching people data.

monday.move: Ask my DPO and the works council representative what we would need before an AI tool may read employee data. Then decide whether the weekly people-metrics summary can be a read-only draft with a human gate.
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO says employee data cannot go in at all, I stop and keep it as an idea
monday.blocker: I have not asked the DPO or the works council yet, and the module did not say how to start that conversation

misconception.why: The module never mentioned roles or headcount. It was about how to build and when not to over-build. I still think roles go first, and I leave without an answer for my leadership team.

one_line: Good rule of thumb: don't use several agents unless you need to. But I had to translate it to people questions myself.
